resolutions.note: Rule: _trigger_price() computes the level in Decimal and FLOORS it to the cent. Decimal because 6.60 * 0.85 is 5.609999999999999 in binary; floor because half a cent of slop is fixed in absolute terms and therefore unbounded in percentage terms as the entry falls. Why it cannot slip either way: flooring can never put the trigger above the exact threshold (no early fire), and no cent-quoted price can land strictly between the floored cent and the exact level (no late fire), so on any price a market can print `price <= trigger` and `price <= exact level` are the same test. Round 1's `round(price, 2)` and its `level + 1e-9` case were dropped: an epsilon on the price is the same unbounded-percentage slop R7 is about, and price-precision mismatch is now T57's problem (adjusted vs unadjusted closes), which is percent-scale.

sweeps.implementer: entries 0.01-999.99, four cent prices probed around each trigger (~400k probes). -15%: 4999 on-grid / 95000 off-grid, 0 early, 0 late. -33.3%: 99 on-grid / 99900 off-grid, 0 early, 0 late. `trigger <= exact decimal level` asserted for every entry in both sweeps.
sweeps.orchestrator: Independently re-run over both grids and both directions at -15% and -33.3% (~800k probes total): 0 fires-early, 0 fires-late. This sweep covered the off-cent-level entries that round 1's verification - by the implementer and by the orchestrator alike - excluded, which is why the widened trigger survived that round.
